document: Requests, Private Payment Lists and Receipts
notes: All hexadecimal is lower case. JSON documents are given as strings; hashes and signatures cover their exact bytes.
Bitcoin only: no case names another asset, the test payment method, or a conversion from another asset.
source names the upstream file and the JSON path of each case; hand_written cases give the rule they follow in basis.
The keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

Members added to upstream cases, naming inputs the checker needs: `recipient_app` (messages), `proof` and `requests` (payee_label_senders), `natural_key_parts` (record_keys). Messages signed again here carry `base`, the upstream message they change; period details in conversion_terms carry `request` and `request_conversion`.

keys.description: The fixed test keys. Each secret is BLAKE3(seed_prefix + seed label), a 32-byte Ed25519 seed; the public key, Pubky ID (z-base-32), App ID (first 16 bytes of BLAKE3 of the signing key, z-base-32), Switch root derive("pubky-switch/v1/scope-root", secret) and naming key derive("pubky-switch/v1/naming", root) follow from it. These keys are published test values and must never hold funds.

certificates.description: Each Paykit app's certificate, signed by its identity key. Every verifier, the Switch's and Paykit's, accepts each.

payee_certificates.description: Spec 3.1, wire 3.1: a payee app's certificate. paykit_request and every paykit_request:<label> require paykit_settlements, so that every payee app, a labelled one included, reads and writes the one mark of each settlement the identity credits (wire 5.7), and paykit_contacts, so that every app that receives as payee holds the identity's lists. accepted are the shop's and the hosted app's certificates of this file's certificates, which hold both beside paykit_request and beside paykit_request:shop1. refused are those certificates with paykit_settlements removed from their scopes, and, last, the shop's with paykit_contacts removed, each with the permissions its scopes need, signed again by bob's identity key: the switch takes each (switch_accepts), and Paykit's verifiers refuse each. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier.

accepted.name: the shop's certificate, paykit_request with paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts
the hosted app's certificate, paykit_request:shop1 with paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts

refused.name: paykit_request and paykit_allowance without paykit_settlements
refused.reason: invalid: paykit_request and every paykit_request:<label> require paykit_settlements

refused.name: paykit_request:shop1 without paykit_settlements
refused.reason: invalid: paykit_request and every paykit_request:<label> require paykit_settlements

refused.name: paykit_request and paykit_allowance without paykit_contacts
refused.reason: invalid: paykit_request and every paykit_request:<label> require paykit_contacts

payer_certificates.description: Spec 3.1, wire 3.1: a paying app's certificate. paykit_pay requires paykit_contacts, so that every paying app reads the deny list and pays no counterparty the user blocked. accepted is Paykit's own phone certificate, which the phone's messages stored in sealed.json carry: the phone's certificate of this file's certificates, which holds paykit_contacts. refused are that certificate with paykit_contacts removed from its scopes, so that it holds paykit_pay and paykit_allowance without paykit_contacts, and the permissions its scopes need, signed again by alice's identity key, and the wallet's certificate of this file's certificates with paykit_pay alone and the permissions paykit_pay needs, signed again by alice's identity key: the switch takes each (switch_accepts), and Paykit's verifiers refuse each. reason is paykit-lib's wording at a Paykit verifier.

accepted.name: Paykit's phone certificate, with paykit_contacts

refused.name: paykit_pay and paykit_allowance without paykit_contacts
refused.reason: invalid: paykit_pay requires paykit_contacts

refused.name: paykit_pay alone
refused.reason: invalid: paykit_pay requires paykit_contacts

amounts.description: Decimal amounts (wire 1.2): valid amounts with the normalized spelling of each, and invalid ones with the reason. The other primitive encodings are the Switch set's encoding.json.

invalid.why: value x 10^18 does not fit in 128 bits

messages.description: Every message kind as sent in v0.2 (Switch wire 4.5, wire 4): the exact JSON bytes, their BLAKE3 hash (refs, request hash), the sender app's signature over lp("pubky-switch/v1/msg", recipient identity, JSON), and the signed plaintext layout sender app ID (16) | signature (64) | u32_be(JSON length) | JSON, before zero padding. payment_request_recurring, payment_period_details, payment_proof_period and payment_request_required_app are the upstream messages of those names written in Bitcoin, since upstream requests them in another asset: each keeps its upstream envelope and is signed again by its sender, with base naming the upstream message.

cases.name: payment_request
cases.note: One-time request with its destination (payment_endpoints) and a payment deadline.

cases.name: payment_request_acceptance
cases.note: Acceptance of the one-time request; refs name the request.

cases.name: payment_request_rejection
cases.note: Rejection with the optional v0.1 reason.

cases.name: payment_request_cancellation
cases.note: Payee cancellation of the recurring request.

cases.name: payment_proof
cases.note: Proof of the one-time request's attempt.

cases.name: private_payment_list
cases.note: Private Payment List with one single-use and one reusable endpoint; version is the pair of the publishing identity generation 1 and counter 12; expires_at 30 days after publishing (wire 4.13).

cases.name: payment_proof_unrequested
cases.note: Proof of a payment without a request, to the single-use list endpoint; no refs.

cases.name: payment_receipt
cases.note: Receipt for the one-time proof; refs name the proof, then the request.

cases.name: resend_request
cases.note: Ask for messages the sender's inbox accepted at one entry's acceptance time.

cases.name: private_payment_list_request
cases.note: Ask the shop app for a newer list than the used one.

cases.name: resend_request_period
cases.note: Ask for the February period's messages of the recurring request: request_hashes names the request, billing_period the period, so the request itself isn't re-sent (wire 4.12).

cases.name: payment_request_labelled
cases.note: One-time request from bob's hosted app, which holds only paykit_request:shop1: it carries the signed label shop1, so the payer's replies go only to bob's apps holding paykit_request or paykit_request:shop1 (wire 4.5).

cases.name: payment_request_acceptance_labelled
cases.note: alice's acceptance of the labelled request: it copies the request's label (wire 4.6).

cases.basis: Paykit wire 4.4, 4.5, 4.9 and 4.10: the upstream message of the same name, its body in Bitcoin and every other member as upstream; refs name the hashes of the messages here.
cases.name: payment_request_recurring
cases.note: Monthly request of 0.0001 btc anchored on January 31; later periods get their destination from period details.

cases.basis: Paykit wire 4.4, 4.5, 4.9 and 4.10: the upstream message of the same name, its body in Bitcoin and every other member as upstream; refs name the hashes of the messages here.
cases.name: payment_period_details
cases.note: Destination for the February period (anchor Jan 31, clamped to Feb 28) of payment_request_recurring.

cases.basis: Paykit wire 4.4, 4.5, 4.9 and 4.10: the upstream message of the same name, its body in Bitcoin and every other member as upstream; refs name the hashes of the messages here.
cases.name: payment_proof_period
cases.note: Payment of the February period by alice's wallet to the period details' destination; refs name the request and the period details it used.

cases.basis: Paykit wire 4.4, 4.5, 4.9 and 4.10: the upstream message of the same name, its body in Bitcoin and every other member as upstream; refs name the hashes of the messages here.
cases.name: payment_request_required_app
cases.note: A one-time request of 0.0025 btc, payable only to the shop app's Lightning endpoints, at a fixed rate of 1.01 for btc-lightning.

conversion_terms.description: Requests and period details with conversion terms or rates, each from a message of messages with its body changed and signed again by the shop. Requests are checked as at check 10. Period details are checked at check 10 and, where a case names request, against payment_request_recurring of messages with its conversion terms replaced by request_conversion, or removed where it is null. A member written as null is read as missing. In a Bitcoin-only series every rate names btc, the requested asset, so period details with rates are never valid against a request.

accepted.basis: Paykit wire 4.4 and 4.9 and specs/payment-conversion.md, as paykit-lib reads them: a request with conversion terms is in an asset of lower-case letters and digits and names identifiers of the form <asset>-<rail>-<format>; per_period terms only on a recurring request; rates are a non-empty array of rates above zero with unique selectors, each <asset> or <asset>-<rail> of such segments, matching the asset, and the rail when it names one, of an identifier the request names. Period details carry payment_endpoints, rates or both; against their request, the period is one of the request's, rates come only under per_period terms, and no rate is for the requested asset, bare or rail-qualified.

A payer's reply with a label needs paykit_request or paykit_request:<label> for that label at the recipient; one without needs paykit_request. reason is the prototype's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

cancellation_roles.description: Wire 4.1 check 8, 4.3, 4.8, spec 3.3: messages.json's payment_request_cancellation, as the shop signs it, without a label, presented with a certificate of the shop's keys (sender_cert) at a certificate of alice's wallet's keys (recipient_cert), each with its scopes changed, its permissions those Paykit's scopes need, and signed again; a certificate holding paykit_pay holds paykit_contacts too, which paykit_pay requires, and one holding paykit_request holds paykit_settlements, which paykit_request requires (spec 3.1). A cancellation's recipient holds the other role than its sender: the payer's goes from paykit_pay to paykit_request, the payee's from paykit_request to paykit_pay. accepted are the two pairings the recipient takes at check 8; refused are paykit_pay to paykit_pay and paykit_request to paykit_request, which it drops there. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

Another protocol's scopes, and the switch permissions they bring, authorize no Paykit message: each kind still needs its Paykit scope, and a resend_request needs a Paykit App, one holding at least one Paykit scope. accepted are messages the wallet takes at check 8, from the shop holding paykit_request, with the paykit_settlements and paykit_contacts it requires, beside chat; refused are those it drops there, from the shop holding chat alone, a certificate Paykit's verifiers take. reason is paykit-lib's wording, of the first check that refuses it.

The receipt about a request confirms proof: messages.json's payment_proof naming payment_request_labelled and copying its label. Each passes check 10, and the details are valid against their request (wire 4.9). accepted are those the payer takes, from paykit_request and from the request's label. refused are those it drops: about a request, from another label or from a label about an unlabelled request, which pass check 8 and are dropped where the payer reads the request, a payer request record holding such a receipt or cancellation being invalid; and a receipt naming no request from a labelled scope, dropped at check 8. reason is paykit-lib's wording.

billing_periods.description: Billing Periods (wire 4.4, spec 8.2, specs/allowances.md anchored rule): boundary k = anchor + k * every units, fixed seconds for minute, hour, day and week, a calendar step from the original anchor for month and year, clamped to the target month's last day. Period k = [boundary(k), boundary(k+1)). The first period contains starts_at; the last contains the instant just before ends_at. start_secs is the obligation ID's period start. A message's {starts_at, ends_at} must equal a computed period, compared as instants.

details_rates.description: The rates of period details apply to a payment whose independently verified payment time, from the payment method's evidence, is at or after their start, the details' created_at cut to whole seconds (v0.1's valid_from), and at or before expires_at, all read at millisecond precision with further digits truncated (Switch wire 1.6, wire 4.9; spec 8.2). An evidence time in whole seconds reads as .000. The payee credits a payment at the rates only then; the payer pays by them only while its device clock and its highest verified service time are both at or after their start and before expires_at.

obligations.description: Paykit's derived identifiers (wire 1.5): request hashes, obligation IDs with their blinded inputs, and the terms hash. Obligations are blinded with the naming key of the identity whose switch holds them (this set's keys.json). Inputs refer to this set's keys.json and messages.json. The Switch's identifiers that Paykit's collections and natural keys give are this set's policies, with their policy hashes, and record_keys, with their blinded natural keys and record keys; the App IDs are keys.json's.

policies.description: Wire 1.5, Switch wire 1.5: the policies of Paykit's collections, each with its read scope, its write scopes and its policy hash, hash(lp("pubky-switch/v1/policy", read_scope, u64(n), write_scope_1, ..., write_scope_n)), hashed_bytes_hex being the bytes hashed: the fixed policy of each collection, by its name, permanent policies use the permanent-policy label and append their generation as a u64, or zero for a null generation, and, last, payee_activity's policy for a request labelled shop1. The cases are the reference implementation's policy cases for the shared records the document names under Shared records, which give none for private_list_publications; block_floor, the payer's own floor for blocked counterparties, is not among those records.

cases.name: payee_activity of a request labelled shop1

record_keys.description: Wire 1.5, Switch wire 1.5: the record keys of Paykit's natural keys, each in its collection under its policy, blinded with the naming key of the identity whose switch holds it (identity, keys.json): natural_key (and natural_key_hex) is the natural key, blinded_natural_key its blind, derive("pubky-switch/v1/name", naming_key, natural_key), key_material_hex the input of the record key, lp(collection, blinded_natural_key, policy_hash), and record_key derive("pubky-switch/v1/record", collection, blinded_natural_key, policy_hash). The request hashes are those of messages.json's payment_request, payment_request_recurring (its February period, 1772236800) and payment_request_labelled, whose payee record is under the policy of its label shop1. The last is the settlements bucket of the bitcoin-txid settlement of the payment without a request, its settlement_id, held at bob's switch: settlement_tag_input_hex is lp(settlement ID), blinded_settlement_tag_input its blind, settlement_tag_hex the settlement's tag, derive("paykit/v1/settlement", "tag", blinded_settlement_tag_input), bucket u16_be(tag[0..2]) >> 6, mark_settlement_tag_hex bytes 2 to 13 of the tag, which its mark stores, and natural_key lp(u64(bucket)); occurrence_tag_hex is the first 8 bytes of derive("paykit/v1/settlement", "occurrence", occurrence_blinded_natural_key), the blind of the natural key of the occurrence it was credited to, bob's payee record of that payment. natural_key_parts names the parts of the natural key's lp() (wire 1.5 Natural keys).
